_readme: license: 'open' = Creative Commons or similar open license (check each item); 'free' = free to access but rights reserved (link only, do not copy); 'public' = U.S. government or public-domain archive material (check individual items); 'site' = a page inside The Speaking Lab.

items.title: Exploring Public Speaking (read online)
items.licenseDetail: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; photographs are separately copyrighted
items.description: The primary textbook for this course.
items.relevance: Every module and speech page links to a chapter or section.

items.title: Exploring Public Speaking (download PDF, EPUB, AZW3)
items.licenseDetail: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
items.description: Offline copies of the textbook, including the current version.
items.relevance: Use when you have limited internet access.

items.title: Stand up, Speak out: The Practice and Ethics of Public Speaking
items.licenseDetail: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (original author not credited at the original publisher's request)
items.description: A full open textbook with a strong emphasis on speaking ethics.
items.relevance: A second explanation of any concept in this course.

items.title: Speak Out, Call In: Public Speaking as Advocacy
items.licenseDetail: Open textbook; check the license statement on the site before adapting
items.description: An open text that frames public speaking as advocacy.
items.relevance: Useful for the persuasive speech and civic topics.

items.title: Web Literacy for Student Fact-Checkers
items.licenseDetail: CC BY 4.0
items.description: A practical guide to checking claims online: going upstream, reading laterally, and more.
items.relevance: Section 5.3 of the textbook teaches Caulfield's approach.

items.title: Purdue OWL: MLA Formatting and Style Guide
items.licenseDetail: Free to read; all rights reserved. Link only.
items.description: Examples for MLA in-text citations and Works Cited entries.
items.relevance: Use if your instructor assigns MLA.

items.title: Purdue OWL: APA General Format
items.licenseDetail: Free to read; all rights reserved. Link only.
items.description: APA 7 formatting basics and links to reference examples.
items.relevance: The textbook's Appendix E covers APA; use OWL for more examples.

items.title: OpenLearn free courses
items.licenseDetail: Most courses CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; third-party items excepted. Check each course's acknowledgements.
items.description: Free short courses, including communication and study skills.
items.relevance: Independent learning beyond this course.

items.title: The Public Speaking Open Pedagogy Project
items.provider: University of Kansas graduate pedagogy course, hosted on OEN Manifold
items.licenseDetail: Each item carries its own CC license, mostly BY-NC-SA
items.description: Open speech assignments and classroom activities for delivery, ceremonial, informative, and online speaking.
items.relevance: Instructors: ready-to-adapt activities.

items.title: Library of Congress: Gettysburg Address exhibition
items.licenseDetail: Public domain text; check individual images
items.description: Lincoln's drafts and related photographs.
items.relevance: Featured in Great Speeches.

items.title: National Park Service: Ain't I A Woman? (comparing versions)
items.licenseDetail: U.S. government page; historical texts are public domain
items.description: Both historical versions of Sojourner Truth's 1851 speech with discussion questions.
items.relevance: Featured in Great Speeches; great for source-accuracy discussions.

items.title: JFK Library: Address at Rice University (video)
items.licenseDetail: Video listed as public domain; check captions availability
items.description: Video and transcript of the 1962 Moon speech.
items.relevance: Audience adaptation and making statistics meaningful.

items.title: Miller Center: Presidential Speeches archive
items.licenseDetail: Free to access; check terms before reuse
items.description: Audio and transcripts of presidential speeches; this link opens FDR's First Inaugural.
items.relevance: Listening practice for vocal delivery.

items.title: The American Presidency Project
items.licenseDetail: Free to access
items.description: A large archive of presidential documents; this link opens FDR's address as delivered.
items.relevance: Compare delivered and prepared texts.

items.title: Stanford King Institute: "I Have a Dream"
items.provider: Martin Luther King, Jr. Research and Education Institute
items.licenseDetail: King's words are copyrighted by his estate; read on the site
items.description: History of how the speech developed.
items.relevance: Extemporaneous delivery and allusion.

items.title: NobelPrize.org: Nobel Lectures
items.licenseDetail: Copyrighted; free to read and watch
items.description: Text and video of Nobel lectures, including Malala Yousafzai's.
items.relevance: Acceptance speeches that also persuade.

items.title: Texas Archive of the Moving Image: Barbara Jordan, 1976 keynote
items.provider: Texas Archive of the Moving Image
items.licenseDetail: Free to watch
items.description: Full video from Texas Southern University's Barbara Jordan archives.
items.relevance: Delivery: pace, articulation, and pauses.

items.title: Creative Commons: BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
items.description: What the textbook's license allows and requires.
items.relevance: Understanding how open materials may be reused.

items.title: Speech Studio: outline builder
items.description: Build a full outline step by step and download it.
items.relevance: Your main planning tool.

items.title: Textbook Appendix I: Sample outlines and formats
items.licenseDetail: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
items.description: Sample informative and persuasive outlines plus three outline formats (p. 426).
items.relevance: Model outlines to compare with your own.

items.title: Delivery Lab: timer, breathing, pauses
items.description: Practice tools for delivery.
items.relevance: Use before every speech.

items.title: Textbook Chapter 11: Delivery
items.licenseDetail: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
items.description: Methods of delivery, practice strategies, and an acting instructor's advice on the voice (p. 222).
items.relevance: The foundation for the Delivery Lab.

items.title: Visual Aid Lab
items.description: Before-and-after slide decisions.
items.relevance: Use while designing your presentation aid.

items.title: Textbook Chapter 9: Presentation Aids
items.licenseDetail: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
items.description: Functions, types, and design of presentation aids (p. 166).
items.relevance: Design principles for slides.

items.title: Speech Anxiety Toolkit
items.description: Thought-pattern practice, strategies, and a pre-speech checklist.
items.relevance: Use in the days before a speech.

items.title: Textbook Section 1.2: Anxiety and Public Speaking
items.licenseDetail: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
items.description: Where speaking anxiety comes from and how to address it (p. 4).
items.relevance: The basis for the Anxiety Toolkit.
